samples.summary: `ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR` reads inherited Object.prototype keys, so `?error=toString` (or `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`) resolves to a function instead of falling back
samples.evidence: `const ERROR_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = { login_state: ... }` is an ordinary object literal, so `ERROR_MESSAGES["constructor"]` is `Object` and `ERROR_MESSAGES["toString"]` is a function — never `undefined`, so `?? FALLBACK_ERROR` does not fire. React then gets a function as a child of the `role="alert"` div: it logs "Functions are not valid as a React child" and renders an empty alert box, i.e. a refused login with no message at all. The new test added in this delta (`falls back to a generic message for an unknown error code`, login-form.test.tsx:44) exercises exactly this branch but only with `something_new`, so the case is uncovered. Fix: `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ERROR_MESSAGES, error)` or a null-prototype map.

samples.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE=false` on an https deployment silently disables CLI sign-in and drops `__Host-`, with no warning — the same quiet downgrade the new warning was added to prevent
samples.evidence: `secureCookies` returns the configured value before any derivation (line 159-160), and `cliLoginAvailable` (line 216) is `secureCookies(...) || loopbackCallback(...)`. So on an https, non-loopback deployment `COOKIE_SECURE=false` makes `wafflebase login` answer `400 Command-line sign-in requires an https server` and strips `__Host-` from every login cookie, while `warnIfPlainHttpProduction` never runs (it is only reached from the `http://` derivation branch at line 166-169). Neither the README nor self-hosting.md mentions that `COOKIE_SECURE=false` turns off CLI login.

samples.summary: The unset-callback-URL fallback (`NODE_ENV === 'production'` → Secure) still produces the dead-login failure mode the PR describes, and it emits no warning
samples.evidence: Line 170 returns `true` when `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is unset and `NODE_ENV=production` — the shipped Dockerfile case. On a plain-http origin that sets `Secure`/`__Host-` cookies the browser discards, which is exactly the '/login?error=login_state loop' the doc comment above calls a dead login, and `warnIfPlainHttpProduction` is only called from the `http://` branch, so this path is silent. `COOKIE_SECURE=false` is the only escape and nothing points at it at runtime.
